```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

This vignette assumes `NCHS_NAT_PARQUET` is set, on the machine running it, to
a sharded Parquet directory written by [natality_pack()] -- see
`vignette("nchsNatality")` (or `inst/adrs/`) for how that directory relates
to `NCHS_NAT_PATH` and the raw fixed-width file it was packed from.

```{r check}
library(nchsNatality)

parquet_dir <- nchs_nat_parquet_dir()
## the same structural check read_natality() itself uses to decide whether
## NCHS_NAT_PARQUET is usable -- see inst/adrs/0004-validation-and-fallback.md
have_parquet <- nzchar(parquet_dir) && nchsNatality:::.valid_parquet_dir(parquet_dir)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = have_parquet)
```

```{r announce, echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE, results = "asis"}
if (have_parquet) {
  cat("`NCHS_NAT_PARQUET` is set to a valid directory on this machine ",
      "(`", parquet_dir, "`); the rest of this vignette runs against it.\n", sep = "")
} else {
  cat("`NCHS_NAT_PARQUET` is not set to a valid directory on this machine ",
      "(got `", if (nzchar(parquet_dir)) parquet_dir else "<unset>", "`), ",
      "so the remaining code chunks are shown but not evaluated here. ",
      "Set `NCHS_NAT_PARQUET` to a directory written by `natality_pack()` ",
      "and re-knit to run them.\n", sep = "")
}
```

```{r libs}
library(dplyr)
```

## 1. `read_natality()` resolves to Parquet automatically

With `NCHS_NAT_PARQUET` set, `read_natality()` needs no `file` argument at
all -- it queries the shards via DuckDB instead of scanning the fixed-width
text, and the result is the same `data.table` shape either way (see
`?read_natality`).

```{r read}
dt <- read_natality(cols = c("DOB_MM", "MAGER", "SEX", "COMBGEST", "DBWT"))
nrow(dt)
```

A `data.table` is also a `data.frame`, so ordinary dplyr verbs work on it
directly once it is in memory:

```{r tidy-in-memory}
dt |>
  label_natality(cols = "SEX") |>
  filter(!is.na(DBWT), !is.na(COMBGEST)) |>
  group_by(SEX) |>
  summarise(n = n(), mean_dbwt = mean(DBWT), mean_gestation = mean(COMBGEST))
```

## 2. Tidy queries that never materialize the full resource

`read_natality()` is convenient, but it still pulls the requested columns for
every record into memory. For an aggregate over the *whole* resource -- all
shards, all records -- it is more efficient to let dplyr push the
filter/group-by/summarise down to the Parquet files themselves, via
[arrow::open_dataset()], and only pull back the (small) aggregated result
with `collect()`.

```{r arrow-setup}
library(arrow)

## name the shards explicitly -- the directory also holds storage.csv,
## which open_dataset() would otherwise try to read as data
nat <- open_dataset(Sys.glob(file.path(parquet_dir, "*.parquet")))
nat
```

```{r lazy-query}
by_month <- nat |>
  filter(DBWT != 9999) |>              # NCHS sentinel for "not stated"
  group_by(DOB_MM) |>
  summarise(n = n(), mean_dbwt = mean(DBWT)) |>
  arrange(DOB_MM) |>
  collect()

by_month
```

`by_month` is an ordinary tibble; everything up to `collect()` ran against
the Parquet shards, not against an in-memory copy of the whole file.

## 3. Combining the two

A common pattern: scan the resource for a filtered, aggregated slice with
`arrow`/`dplyr`, then relabel the few columns that matter for a figure or
table with [label_natality()].

```{r combine}
by_sex <- nat |>
  filter(DBWT != 9999) |>
  group_by(SEX, DPLURAL) |>
  summarise(n = n(), mean_dbwt = mean(DBWT), mean_age = mean(MAGER)) |>
  collect() |>
  label_natality(cols = c("SEX", "DPLURAL"))

by_sex
```
